flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
So I, my journey started right after high school where I joined an after-school program as a coach. I started off from the very bottom and I liked it so much I actually went into child development major. And from there I proceeded to get promoted to what would be like an assistant director and then to a director for an after-school program. I did that for about six years and then I moved from California to Virginia and that's actually where I started my preschool journey. And I was a lead for about two years at a four-year-old, yeah four-year-old and then from there again I got promoted to assistant director. And then I just, I kept growing. I mean I think it's important because these children need such a strong base to grow from. That I've gotten both sides of it. I've gotten from me having to build that base when they're two or four to the kids that either got the base or did not during school age. So I know it's super important for the social-emotional development to happen from zero to five.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you received feedback you didn’t expect or didn’t fully agree with. What happened next?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q6 Attempt 1]
When, I like to believe I do get, I do receive criticism correctly, but there is times where we just kind of have to agree to disagree. What we ended up doing was compromising. It was about the stage of the child that they should be in, me versus another teacher. And I believe that they were exactly where they're supposed to be and they thought that the child was not fully to their potential. So what we ended up doing was giving that student, I guess like extra support on some things that she noticed. And then I also made sure that she realized, I gave her support on trainings on child development as well.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something didn’t go as planned at work and your role in it. How did you handle the responsibility piece?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q7 Attempt 1]
I guess whenever you plan an activity or you plan a lesson plan, you imagine and you envision something that is not necessarily going to come true. Sometimes the students are not really into the activity or maybe it took less time than you had imagined. My part was to, I always have backup activities, so whenever something like that does happen, I pivot and sometimes I revert back to either the basics because it was too hard or if it was too easy, I go to my pocket activities that I have for just extra time.
